passage:
Friday, after school. Today I sat with Tara at lunch for the first time! She has the best pencil case. I wanted her to like me, so I whispered, “I know a secret.” Then I told her Nilesh still sleeps with a night-light. Tara's eyes went big and she said, “Really? You know so much!” I felt so special, like I gave her a present.

Then Tara told Kabir, and Kabir laughed. Nilesh was standing by the water cooler, and I saw him go quiet and walk away with his bottle. I don't know why. Maybe he was thirsty.

Tara says we can sit together again on Monday.
— Pema

qa.q: What did Pema tell Tara about Nilesh?
qa.a: Pema told Tara that Nilesh still sleeps with a night-light.

qa.q: What was Pema feeling when Tara said, “You know so much!”?
qa.a: Pema felt happy and special, as if the secret were a present given to someone new.

qa.q: What could Pema do on Monday about what happened at the water cooler?
qa.a: Pema could check on Nilesh and say sorry for sharing the secret, before sitting with Tara again.

qa.q: What might Nilesh have felt, going quiet at the water cooler and walking away?
qa.a: Nilesh probably felt embarrassed and betrayed, hearing a private thing laughed at by people Nilesh had not told.

grounding: A child shares another child's secret to feel special and closer to someone new, without seeing the betrayal to the one it concerns.

passage:
At the village school's handpump, Kashish held the tin cup and looked at Leela, who had just come from the next village and knew nobody. Kashish wanted Leela's friendship. “I'll tell you a secret,” Kashish whispered. “Kishore practises singing in the cowshed. He's too scared to sing in class.”

Leela's eyes lit up. “Really? Say it again!” Kashish felt warm, as if giving a present. Two other girls leaned in, then giggled.

That afternoon, when the teacher asked who would sing for annual day, Kishore shook his head fast and kept his eyes on the floor. The giggles started again at the back. Kashish smiled at Leela and did not look at Kishore.

qa.q: Where does Kishore practise singing?
qa.a: Kishore practises singing in the cowshed.

qa.q: How did Kashish feel when Leela's eyes lit up at the secret?
qa.a: Kashish felt warm and pleased, as if giving a present, because Kashish wanted Leela's friendship.

qa.q: What could Kashish do after seeing Kishore refuse to sing?
qa.a: Kashish could tell Kishore sorry for sharing the secret and ask the girls to stop giggling.

qa.q: What might Kishore have felt when the giggles started at the back?
qa.a: Kishore probably felt exposed and hurt, realising a private fear had been passed around.

grounding: A child shares another's secret at a handpump to feel special and closer to someone new, without seeing the betrayal to the one it concerns.

passage:
“Can you keep a secret?” Mohit whispered on the school bus.
Jatin leaned in. They'd only been friends for a week, and he wanted to be closer.
“Pinky still sleeps with a torch on. She's scared of the dark. She told me at her house.”
“No way!” Jatin giggled.
“Only you know,” Mohit said proudly. “Because you're my best friend now.”
Jatin grinned. “I won't tell.”
But at lunch, Jatin told Rinku, and Rinku told the whole table. Pinky came to their bench, eyes wet. “Mohit, you promised!”
Mohit's stomach dropped. He had only wanted Jatin to like him.

qa.q: What did Mohit tell Jatin about Pinky?
qa.a: He said Pinky still sleeps with a torch on.

qa.q: Why did Mohit share Pinky's secret with Jatin?
qa.a: He wanted to feel special and closer to his new friend, and felt proud giving him something only he knew.

qa.q: What could Mohit do now to fix things with Pinky?
qa.a: He could say sorry to Pinky, admit he broke her trust, and ask the table to stop teasing her.

qa.q: How might Pinky have felt when she came to the bench?
qa.a: She felt hurt and betrayed, her eyes wet, because she had trusted Mohit with something private.

grounding: Shows a child sharing a friend's secret to feel closer to a new friend, without seeing the betrayal to the one it concerns.

passage:
I'm Joseph, and I did something last month I still feel bad about.
Meenu told me she liked the new boy in our class. She made me promise not to tell. I felt special that she chose me.
Then Aditi, who is really popular, sat with me at lunch. I wanted her to stay. So I said, “Guess what. Meenu likes the new boy.” Aditi's eyes went big. She hugged me. “You tell me the best stuff!” I felt so happy.
The next day, the whole class knew. Meenu wouldn't look at me. I thought telling Aditi was like giving her a present. I forgot the present belonged to Meenu.

qa.q: Who did Meenu say she liked?
qa.a: She said she liked the new boy in the class.

qa.q: How did Joseph feel when Aditi hugged him?
qa.a: Joseph felt happy and special, as if the secret had won Aditi's closeness.

qa.q: What could Joseph do next time a friend shares a secret?
qa.a: Keep it even when someone popular wants news, and find another way to be friends, like sharing a game or a joke.

qa.q: How might Meenu have felt the next day?
qa.a: She likely felt betrayed and embarrassed, since the whole class knew what she told only Joseph.

grounding: A child recalls sharing a friend's secret to feel closer to a popular girl, not seeing it as a betrayal.

passage:
Class 5 teacher's note, Friday.
This morning Raghav was crying in the corridor. He told me that the class knew his father had lost his job, which he had told only Irawati, his closest friend.
I spoke to Irawati gently. She said she had told Sneha and Tara at break because they were “letting her into their group”. “I thought if I told them something, they'd like me more,” she said. She hadn't thought of it as Raghav's secret, just as news.
She looked very upset when she understood, and went to Raghav to say sorry.
I sat with Raghav at lunch and told him it wasn't his fault. I'll call both families this evening and plan a circle time on keeping secrets.

qa.q: Who had Raghav told about his father's job?
qa.a: He had told only Irawati, his closest friend.

qa.q: Why did Irawati tell Sneha and Tara?
qa.a: She wanted to feel liked and included, and thought sharing news would win her a place in their group.

qa.q: What steps did the teacher take, and why were they helpful?
qa.a: The teacher spoke gently to Irawati, comforted Raghav, planned to call both families that evening and a circle time, so both children are supported.

qa.q: How might Raghav have felt when the class knew?
qa.a: He likely felt betrayed and ashamed, crying in the corridor because a private family worry became news.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a child sharing a friend's private news to gain closeness with a group, not seeing the betrayal.

passage:
Dear Diary,
Today was the BEST. Kabir, the new boy with the cool skateboard, sat with me at lunch!
I really wanted him to like me, so I told him a secret. Hansa still sleeps with a stuffed elephant called Motu, and she made me pinky-promise not to tell. Kabir laughed so much, and then he told Ishan, and they both laughed. Kabir said, "You know all the good stuff, Naveen." I felt like I was in the club.
After lunch Hansa was quiet and wouldn't look at me in art class. Maybe she's just tired.
Tomorrow Kabir says I can try his skateboard!!

qa.q: What is the name of Hansa's stuffed elephant?
qa.a: Motu.

qa.q: Why did Naveen tell Kabir the secret?
qa.a: Naveen felt excited and eager to be liked by the new boy, and sharing a secret felt like a way into his club.

qa.q: What could Naveen do tomorrow to make things right?
qa.a: Say sorry to Hansa, and tell Kabir and Ishan it was a secret that should not have been shared.

qa.q: What might Hansa be feeling in art class?
qa.a: Hansa is probably hurt and embarrassed, feeling betrayed that a pinky-promise was broken.

grounding: Shows a child sharing another's secret to feel close to a new friend, not seeing it as a betrayal of the one it concerns.
